decisions.example: none — 7c3e's chrome mention and 8d05's label force the same file name in the same place above the code; no page can satisfy one and break the other.
none — the ochre of an assumed diagram node is the palette's assumed colour; changing either changes the other.
none — the ochre of the why in the pane is the same assumed colour; one swatch, three surfaces.
none — node and pane take their ochre from the same rule; no input parts them.
none — clicking an assumed node selects and narrows exactly as clicking a real node; the machinery cannot tell them apart.
hovering a code span owned by two sentences lights two diagram nodes; hovering a diagram node lights one node and its spans — different trigger, different lit set.
hovering node a, joint owner of a span with b, lights b under co-owner lighting; code-hover lighting fires only from code and says nothing here.
a renderer that deletes unowned spans outright still narrows the code but draws no fold and counts nothing.
over the same fold the gutter prints a source index like 37 while the fold prints a quantity like 12 lines.
a map where every span has exactly one owner still needs the full index while joint ownership changes nothing there.
a renderer that alphabetises the project list decides an order — breaking render-only — while still printing every item exactly as emitted.
on first load no click has happened: silence empties the panes while selection has not fired at all.
a tooltip that shows the why while the pane prints only the word assumed satisfies why-text and violates pane-why.
a top-left bar naming the project with no caret is legal chrome under project-bar and opens nothing under project-caret.
the rename to human_code moved code only in the projects-view template that prints the field; the disk read of the list kept every byte.
